I strictly follow a Jain diet, and I make it a point to clearly mention this every single time I order. Despite that, I’ve been served regular food containing onion, garlic, etc., on three different occasions. What’s even worse is that when I double-checked with the waiter, he confidently assured me that the food was Jain — only for me to later realize that it wasn’t.

This isn’t just a casual mistake — it’s a serious breach of trust, especially for those of us who follow dietary rules for religious reasons. And now I’m left wondering how many times I may have unknowingly consumed non-Jain food in the past.

The first time I complained, the manager offered to cancel the item from the bill. By the third time, I made it clear that this solution was not acceptable anymore. The manager told me they were busy due to a crowd and would call back with a resolution — but they never did.

This experience has truly shaken the trust I had in this restaurant. If you follow strict dietary guidelines — whether for religious, health, or personal reasons — I urge you to double and triple check your food before eating here. And even then, there are no guarantees.

["{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=The Bombay Earth is one of the restaurants out of the many others in the premises of Eskay resorts ,it's a pure vegetarian restaurant which offers you some amazing mocktails and some decent cocktails.
The presentation of mocktails is really something to look out for and some decent work done in the cocktail as well.
The restaurant is quite spacious and usually people come over here in groups for kitty parties and normal dine in .
They offer membership to the resort and also discounts are offered to their members as well on their food bills.

The Vibes of this place is really positive and soothing , the staff is welcoming and sweet to talk.
They gave us some really good suggestions for trying some amazing stuff especially the spinach smoothies which was a shocker to me as I hate spinach , but it turned out to be a blunder .

What we tried goes out like this -

▶️Mocktails
1) Cranberry kiss - from presentation to the taste , from edible flowers at the top to the cranberry and grenadine taste along with the orange juice Everything was perfectly balanced in this amazing Mocktail , highly recommended 🔴

2)Spinach Smoothie - I literally was surprised to hear that it's a spinach smoothie but by the looks it looks decent and the amazin artwork of lemon at the top for presentation was really worth the wait , the mixture of spinach and some kiwi literally didn't make it feel as if I was having spinach smoothie , something which was really worth a try ..

▶️Cocktails
1) Choco Martini -good old cocktail made with coffee liqueur mixed with coffee powder topped with whiskey...every sip was refreshing when coffee liqueur hits your palate

2) Activated Batman - something unique and must try drink ...edible charcoal shaked with whiskey garnish with pineapple sticks...taste was unique as were the ingredients in it

▶️Appetizers
1)Kung pao Potatoes - Chinese style potato fries tossed in Kung pao sauce garnished with sesame seeds... perfectly balanced sweet and sourtaste hits the right note.

2) Tandoori platter - a platter consisting of all the options in the menu from cauliflower to baby potatoes to mushrooms to baby corn Everything was available in the Platter , Different exotic vegetables marinated with different sauces and made up on tandoor , achari aloo was my favourite marinated dish, and so was the baby corn , not to forget the paneer was also delicious the achari seekh kebabs can be a lil juicy as they became a lil dry  , but a good blend very soft and yummy , overall a good platter .

▶️Main course
1)Pot rice -  a mixture of many veggies and loads of rice though the presentation is something that can be worked on the tomatoes at the side make it look more Indian otherwise the taste of the dish is really good to have , the veggies are diced nicely and make it really healthy and a flavour full potrice , enough for two people quite fullfilling and  worth the penny.

▶️Desserts
Mango cream - Seasonal dessert consist of whipped cream mixed with mango juice and garnished with slice of mango slice ,it's the summer special dish and since it's mango season they have mango cream in their dessert section which is presented quite  beautifully and the glass filled with cream and mango juice giving it the sweet and sour taste , making it really delicious and something you should definitely try in the mango special season.highly recommended 🔴

Overall the service is good  , the management is really sweet though they take a lil time which they can improve other then that it's a really good place to look out for , an amazing place for a veggie lover and for someone who wishes to relax and get out of the noise of the city it's a perfect hideout place ., name_person=Sagar Kantharia Foodie_mumbaikar7}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=5 years ago, review=Recently visited this amazing outlet at eskay resorts called the Bombay earth. We had a table reservation for 9:45 PM and arrived by 9:55 PM. Despite being just 10 minutes late, we were made to wait another 10 minutes before being seated—even though we could clearly see 4–5 empty tables inside. This initial delay set the tone for what turned out to be an underwhelming evening.

Once seated, we weren’t provided with menus until we asked for them. After deciding on our soups and starters, no server approached us for over 10 minutes, prompting me to personally request someone to take our order. There was no water on the table, and even after requesting it, the server simply forgot—walking past our table multiple times to serve others. Eventually, I had to approach someone who seemed to be the manager, only to be told, repeatedly, that “the staff is busy” and we needed to “co-operate.” Frankly, it doesn’t take much effort to bring menus, take an order, or serve water—basic expectations at any restaurant.

As for the food:

Soups: The Manchow soup was lukewarm and seemed like it came straight from the buffet, with soggy fried noodles on the side. The Tomato soup, on the other hand, had a nice basil flavor and was decent.

Starters: The Paneer Chilly was flavorful and enjoyable. Among the non-veg options, the Korean Fried Chicken had an odd fishy smell, although the sauce was good. The Pan Fried Chicken Momos were tasty, though the accompanying dip was overly sweet.

Main Course: The Chicken Tikka Masala and assorted breads were well-prepared and satisfying. However, the Chicken Biryani was disappointing—bland and lacking any real depth of flavor. The vegetarian mains—Vegetable Stir Fry in Hot Garlic Sauce and Pink Pasta—were good but took an unusually long time to arrive.

Mocktails: We tried the No-jito, a twist on the classic mojito, which didn’t stand out, and the Guava Mary, which was refreshing and enjoyable.

No desserts were ordered, mainly because by the end of the meal, our patience was running thin.

Overall, the dining experience was marred by disorganized service, inattentive staff, and inconsistent food quality. While a few dishes did manage to impress, they weren’t enough to outweigh the frustrating delays and lack of basic hospitality. For a restaurant that seems to take pride in its offerings, the service fell severely short.

I’ve been visiting Café Bae in Lower Parel for the past three years, and over time, I’ve tried pretty much everything on their menu. It’s been a go-to spot for casual meals, and while the food has always been decent, there have been a few changes worth noting.

Earlier, Café Bae felt like a solid pocket-friendly option – good food at fair prices. But lately, the prices have gone up, and with that, the overall value feels a bit off. The space is quite compact and tends to get crowded, which can make the experience feel a bit cramped, especially during peak hours.

But the worst part was the billing experience:

Billing Ethics: Manipulative and unclear.

- Prawns Bhujane

- Solkadi

In the often-cacophonous theatre of Borivali West, where every corner screams for attention, there exists a quiet, graceful pause—a Parsi sanctuary. To call this establishment merely a café is to mistake a perfectly cut diamond for a simple stone. This is a treat, yaar, a small revelation wrapped in an ambience of serene, unpretentious class.

It is a place where the air itself seems infused with generational grace, the kind that whispers of old Bombay, good recipes, and true hospitality. Everything about the setting—the light, the clean lines, the subtle decorative flourishes—suggests that one should simply sit, sigh, and prepare for a genuine moment of peace.

A Culinary Revelation: The Mexican Manna
While the atmosphere is a gentle balm for the soul, let us not mince words, dikra: the food is the star, the crescendo of the entire visit. You can, and should, close your eyes and point randomly to the menu; you will not find fault. But if one must declare a favorite, it is with dramatic emphasis that I must praise their pizzas.

And among them? The Mexican Pizza is not just food; it is a philosophy. It’s an unlikely, perfect marriage of Parsi punctuality and Aztec spice, a fiery yet balanced canvas of flavor that dances on the palate and leaves you wondering why you haven't dedicated your life to consuming it daily. A testament to a kitchen that respects tradition but isn't afraid to give it a joyful, spicy kick.

The Triumph of the Sweet Smile

Yet, even after the last crumb of that incredible Mexican feast has vanished, the lasting impression, the true elixir of this Borivali gem, is the management.

You know the types, don’t you? The proprietors in other establishments who stride through the dining room with the air of an emperor addressing his least favorite vassals, whose very presence makes you feel guilty for existing, as if your patronage is a tiresome formality.

Here, we find the sublime opposite. The humble manager is a lesson in human decency. His kindness is not a trained customer service routine; it is an aura. He moves with an earnest sweetness, his smile a genuine beacon that will cling to you long after you’ve left the place. It's the unmistakable, unwavering elegance of Parsi hospitality—a profound, quiet pride in making you feel welcome, safe, and utterly valued.

This gentleman’s demeanor is not just good for business; it is good for the soul. He is a testament to the belief that true class resides not in the décor, but in the effortless, respectful treatment of one’s guests. This particular Smokin' Joe's outlet is located on a very isolated road, which already makes it less convenient to access. While the food quality is acceptable and meets the standards of the brand (earning it 3 stars in the food category), the rest of the experience was significantly disappointing.
Atmosphere (1/5 Stars)
The dining area is a major drawback. It is confined to a small, tightly closed room with extremely limited seating, accommodating only about 10-15 people. This configuration feels claustrophobic and does not offer a comfortable dining experience.
Service (1/5 Stars)
The service was the most frustrating aspect. Due to the isolated location and very low foot traffic, the waiters appeared completely uninterested and disengaged. I had to repeatedly call them over for every request and to place each subsequent order. This lack of attentiveness severely detracted from the experience.
Final Verdict
If you are passing by and absolutely need a quick, reliable pizza from this brand, the food will suffice. However, the combination of the isolated location, cramped atmosphere, and genuinely poor, inattentive service means I cannot recommend dining in at this location. Management needs to address the service standards immediately.

The restaurant is spacious with a mini and a full sized bar. The ambiance is super bright with tribal decor touch. Loved the colours used everywhere and every corner looks really beautiful. The seatings are arranged nicely and options for all size of groups are available. They also have DJ section and a dedicated space for live events.

The menu contains global dishes with sone traditional Indian food being available too. Loved the menu as you get everything from sushi to chicken tikka is available in their menu. Prices are at par with similar type of brands and the quantity served is nice. Also they do run dining offers so check online before visiting.

We went here for late lunch and kitchen service was decent but table service was haywire as the staff was super confused as they were booked for a private party at 6PM so I think they were under immense pressure as they kept on switching dishes on different tables. However staff Sandeep tried his best to make the table service smooth.

What We Had -
APPETISERS~
Butter Paneer Potli -
Butter paneer stuffed in a potli, fried to perfection but not oily, and served with a makhani dip. What I liked most was that it wasn’t sweet, the flavors of spices and onions really stood out, making the dish taste perfect.

Herb Crusted Truffle Parmesan Chicken Tikka -
One of the classy version of chicken tikka which tasted amazing. Perfectly grilled juicy chicken done in green spices topped with cheese with light truffle oil and with walnuts on the top tasted perfect. Everything in this tasted superb and you should definitely try this.

Golden Prawn Tempura Roll -
Again one of the best sushi experiences. Their portion is 5 pieces so you will definitely crave more. Crunchy tempura, fresh prawns, spicy sauce and everything in this sushi was perfect.

MAINS~
Wild Mushroom & Truffle Cacio E Pepe -
Man. This was one of the best pasta I have ever had. Earthy flavours due to mushrooms and truffle oil. Perfectly done spaghetti with crunchy veggies and the watery cheese sauce was outstanding. Try it to believe it.

Prawn Ghee Pepper Roast with Tadka Lemon Coriander Rice -
Fresh prawns in ghee roast gravy tasted good. The rice went nicely however I am not a fan of whole coriander hence full marks for gravy.

DESSERT~
Slow Baked Chocolate Bar -
This wasn’t that great as the chocolate used was not that tasty.

MOCKTAILS~
Black & Yellow.
Tropical Delight.

All in all, for veg Options are limited and not worth paying so much for., name_person=Sachi Gandhhi}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=Illuminati

“Beautiful things and Delicious food is priceless.” It’s a thought come to my mind when I’ve visited newly opened place in BKC named Illuminati. This place surprises me in my first visit. As you entered the place, it’s a different world altogether.

This place certainly raises the bar chicness and opulence. With all positive vibes and great hospitality Illuminati won accolades.

The place lit with beautiful white lights, classy décor and huge bar. They have a wide collection of Alcohol and wines.

The amazing indulgence of spices and the flavors has made me their fan. The varied menu has really tempted my taste buds and taken it to a niche.

So, first let’s start with cocktails and then food.

Prisoner: Vodka based (kettle one) with Galangal and Lemongrass. Loved the freshness and sweet taste because of lemongrass.

Blue Fairy: Jim Beam + Blueberry + Blue Pea Bitters + Orange slice. Looks amazing but tasted less of alcohol. Maybe not stirred well, still can give a try.

Believer: Believe me, it’s the best one among all three. Kettle One Vodka+ Chamomile spiced Apple + Thyme. Really amazing. This was smooth, fresh and bit different.

Quick Steamed Rawas Xiao Xing: Loved the balance. Bold flavors. Very smooth texture. Presentation is beautiful. Rawas fish is served with Xiao Xing wine. Overall colourful and made well. Do try.

Tokyo Chicken Karrage: This looks amazing and tasted so good, crunchy. You can taste both sweet and spicy at the same time. I could actually feel the distinct flavors yet intact.

Tempura Prawn: It delectably delights you. One of the best tempura prawn sushi I had in recent time. Tasted lovely.

Chicken and Bok Choy: It was simply great. Bok Choi is a type of Chinse Cabbage. Minced Chicken and Bok Choy has a generous stuffing. Served hot. Do try.

Honey Sesame Chicken Bowl: I still cannot get over this. The star dish of the day. Diced chicken tossed in sticky sesame soy with a bit of 5 pickled chillies. All the herbs intact and served with Jasmine rice was a delicious treat to my gluttony.

The Decadent Cake French Toast: Not too sweet. But not to be miss for sure.

Time and again I would just sing praises for this absolutely amazing place which makes sure to lure its patron and woo them with delicious offerings.

P.S: The review is strictly depending on my personal experience.

Food: 5/5

Décor: 5/5

Leopold Cafe is one of Mumbai’s oldest and most famous cafés, founded in 1871 and located on Colaba Causeway — right across from the Colaba Police Station. It’s a cultural landmark as well as a popular hangout for tourists, locals, and fans of the novel Shantaram.

The café also carries historical significance because it was one of the spots attacked during the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks, and some bullet marks remain preserved as a memorial.

My recent visit to Myra Dining and Bar was nothing short of phenomenal, and it has instantly become one of my favorite spots. The entire experience, from the service to the food, was absolutely perfect and deserves a wholehearted five stars.

Service (5/5):
From the moment we stepped in, we were treated with such warm hospitality. The staff was incredibly attentive, professional, and courteous. They were knowledgeable about the menu, offered great recommendations, and ensured our glasses were never empty. The service was prompt without ever feeling rushed, striking the perfect balance that truly elevates a dining experience.

Food (5/5):
The food was the star of the show! Each dish we ordered was a masterpiece of flavour and presentation.

Chicken Mastani Kebab: This was an absolute revelation. The chicken was incredibly tender and succulent, coated in a rich, creamy, and flavourful marinade that simply melted in the mouth. A must-try for any kebab lover.

Bombil Chilly Dry: As a fan of seafood, I was blown away by this dish. The Bombil was perfectly crispy on the outside while remaining delicate and soft inside. Cheese Garlic Naan: The perfect companion to our meal. It was soft, fluffy, and oozing with the perfect amount of cheese and garlic flavour.

Desserts (Custard and Brownie with Ice Cream): The perfect end to a perfect meal. The Custard was classic, creamy, and silky smooth with just the right level of sweetness. The Brownie with Ice Cream was pure indulgence – a warm, fudgy, and decadent brownie perfectly complemented by a scoop of cold, creamy ice cream.

Overall:
Myra Dining and Bar is a fantastic establishment that gets everything right. ["{guided_block={}, time_line=7 years ago, review=Located near Citylight theater, Ram Punjab was renovated a couple of years ago to get a more upmarket feel, while still maintaining pocket friendly rates. The ambience is not great, it's not what you would call a family friendly place, though nothing like a desi bar, and it does get noisy when crowded. We opened our innings with Smirnoff, and the first starter was Murg Koliwada. They're essentially chicken nuggets, crispy outer layer, delicious meat on the inside, I strongly recommend this one. Murg Sholey Kebab was our next starter, which is chicken kebabs covered in egg fluff. The fluff tastes good only when genuinely hot, so I suggest licking off that first, and then attacking the chicken which was very tender, a little on the sweeter side. With the vodka done we now had rum running down our throats in the form of the all time favourite Old Monk. For the mains we ordered Murg Patiala (what's with everything being named "Murg"!) with Butter Roti. The rotis have enough butter on them to give you a heart attack by just looking at them, but then that's also what makes them so pleasurable for the taste buds. Murg Patiala is chicken and gravy in an omelette, and I totally loved it, a must have in my opinion. Portions served are quite sizeable, so we were too stuffed to have any desserts. The only major downside to this place is the service, which can vary from average to disastrous. From the waiters not being attentive to totally lacking any etiquette, it can be both funny and frustrating. I’ve been a regular at High Point Veg Restaurant, having enjoyed their South Indian specialties like masala dosa, idli vada sambhar, tomato onion uttapam, and rava masala dosa on several past visits. These dishes have consistently delivered the rich flavors and textures one expects from a well-established South Indian eatery. However, my recent foray into their Chinese cuisine left much to be desired, warranting a cautious 2-star rating overall.

A Disappointing Dive into Chinese Cuisine

Lured by multiple glowing reviews on Zomato and Swiggy, I decided to explore the restaurant’s Chinese menu. I ordered three dishes—a rice option, a noodles dish, and a main gravy—to get a comprehensive taste:
•	Burnt Garlic Noodles: Despite the intriguing name, these noodles turned out to be bland, with a stale texture that did not live up to the promise of aromatic garlic notes.
•	Veg Fried Rice: Expected to be a flavorful accompaniment, the fried rice was devoid of any significant seasoning or spice, leaving it tasting flat and uninspired.
•	Mushroom Chilly in Schezwan Sauce: Perhaps the most disappointing of all, the mushroom in this dish was undercooked, and the overall preparation lacked the bold flavors characteristic of a well-executed Schezwan sauce.

Overpriced for the Outcome

To add to the disappointment, the final bill was steep relative to both the quality and quantity of the food served. When paying a premium, diners expect a memorable, flavor-rich meal—a standard the Chinese offerings at High Point simply did not meet.

Final Thoughts

While I would have preferred to give zero stars for the Chinese experience, my past positive encounters with their South Indian dishes have compelled me to settle on a 2-star rating overall. In frame – Tandoori missal, tacos missal, aam panha and kharwas.

1) Tandoori missal:  The missal is served with farsan in a small matka in which there is a bowl of charcoal kept for that smokey effect. The missal is on the spicy side, but it is a perfect combination of blended spices, which add in to the delicious taste. The primary ingredient is matki, which is properly cooked and being a sprout also adds up to the whole nutritious value of the Dish.  Also served  2 Pavs, chopped onions, lemon all these additions complement the original taste even better.

It is one of those restaurants in Borivali that continues to feel like home because of its food and hospitality.

This time, we began our meal with a bowl of Chicken Manchow Soup. It was served hot, and I enjoyed how it had a bold, flavorful taste without being overpowering. For starters, we ordered Veg Seekh Kebab, Mutton Seekh Kebab, and Chicken Pahadi Tikka. The Veg Seekh Kebab was nice, cooked well, and had the perfect earthy flavour. The Mutton Seekh Kebab was outstanding. It had a silky texture, was well-seasoned, and paired beautifully with the chutney. It was not chewy at all, and I really liked how smooth it felt with every bite. The Chicken Pahadi Tikka was equally good. The chicken was tender, juicy, and cooked with a light smokiness that made it enjoyable.

For the mains, I ordered Jeera Rice with Dal Tadka. The dal had a nice garlic tempering with the right amount of cumin, and together with the rice it felt wholesome and comforting. The Chicken Tikka Masala came with soft pieces of chicken in a thick gravy that had a good balance of spices. It went really well with the Tandoori Roti, which was crisp on the edges and soft in the middle. The Chicken Triple Schezwan Fried Rice was the last dish. It was mildly spiced, had a smoky taste from the wok, and the flavours were balanced in a way that made it enjoyable till the last bite.

As we were about to finish, we couldn’t resist ordering the Chicken Masala Lollipop, which has always been a family favorite. It was crispy, spicy, and coated beautifully with sauce. It was the highlight of the evening. The chicken inside was fresh and well-cooked, and every bite reminded me why I have loved this dish here for years.

The food at Silver Coin Family Restaurant and Bar is consistently good, and the staff make the experience even better. They are polite, attentive, and always welcoming. This restaurant is more of a family place, and the presence of a bar only adds to the variety without taking away from its warm atmosphere.

Quality - 4/5
Quantity - 4/5
Service - 4.2/5
Price - ₹5000 for 8 people

Been reviewing since a long time and never have I ever gave such a terrific feedback to a restaurant that's good for nothing !

THE BISLERI WE ORDERED WAS THE ONLY ORDER WE LIKED AT THIS PLACE

Starting with the ambience, you will surely love this place if you go for looks and show off ! It has a dedicated space for kids to play but that is only when you want to go and try their food thats good for nothing !

So as usual, we ordered Masala Papad - Rating is 0.5 out of 5 because the Papad was just dripped out from oil and it had no masala as a topping, only sev, some tomato and onions along with 1.5-2 leaves of coriander ! They should change the name to Oily Masala Papad instead !

Secondly, we ordered Paneer Lababdar - In the picture, you will be able to see 17-18 chopped pieces of almonds, never have I ever seen this in a Paneer Lababdar recipe. Remember about these almonds, I'll tell you about it later.

Sorry youtube chefs if I missed out this part of recipe but the color, the gravy, the content itself was 0.1 out of 5 because the paneer was oil fried for the starters we order like Paneer Chilly but as this might be the Chefs first time to make Paneer Lababdar, he had to do the experiment on us ! I never used Fork and Spoon to cut a Paneer into 2 pieces, this time I did !

Remember I told you about the almonds ? They dissapeared when the vegetable was served to us, we were 3, one of the guy had a luck to eat 4-5 pieces, the rest is mistery !

Coming to the taste, don't know what was inside, one cannot guess what it was, the gravy was nothing but something that I cannot even express in words ! If you could say, it had a taste of tomato gravy ? No, it didnt. If you say it had something related to onions and coriander mixture ? No. Don't know what it was but I never ate Paneer Lababdar this bad ! Sorry I do not want to disrespect Food but the Restaurant, the Owner or anyone who handles the kitchen, must rethink about the chefs !

We order 1 butter roti each and that was all ! They do not serve Cold Drinks as they have Mocktails which I am sure would be another disappointment ! Thanks BISLERI to save us at some point !

We paid the bill and we left, not returning again to this place !

❌ Not Suggesting this place ❌

After this trauma, we went to MK Chinese Resturant near Nalasopara East D-Mart - Check the review on my profile !

Located in Vile Parle East, this restaurant and bar serves some amazingly fresh and quality dishes. The primary cuisine served is North Indian and Chinese. They also have Mangalorean dishes on the menu which are a must try. They have a nice bar with a wide variety of drinks to choose from.

Cindrella has orange juice and fresh lime which makes it very refreshing.

The food we had was all very good in terms of quality and quantity. I would rate it a value for money place.

Coriander Chicken Dry was a Chinese appetizer, this was again very good. Herbaceous flavour with garlic and spring onions. Again well cooked Chicken. Very satisfying.

For the main course we had Chicken Ghee Roast with Neer Dosa. My favourite and everything was perfect. Must have when here. Highly recommended.

The Cheese Garlic Naan here is not the usual Naan with the Garlic and Cheese outside. Here it's stuffed inside and is very wholesome.
We had Chicken Betabi which is a red gravy similar to Butter Chicken in many ways with shredded chicken in a luscious velvety gravy.

For dessert we had a sizzling walnut brownie with ice cream. This was fresh and well made.

This place even has outdoor seating which is accessible only post rains. I am totally in awe of the simplicity and the no nonsense kind of approach to serving good quality food.

I am totally coming back here again with my gang for a great meal.

"The House you want to be at"

I have been through this lane quite a few times but never actually noticed this place until today. The restaurants on this lane have a small entrance so they are hard to notice if you are passing by but they are grand like this one. From the outside it appears that it can accommodate only a handful of people but when you step in you can see the actual picture. They have a lower outdoor seating, a lower indoor seating, an upper outdoor seating and an upper indoor seating.

The coziest and the most house-like feeling is the upper indoor seating - It is made like "The House" and has different types of tables. The lower outdoor seating is the most happening with a few high tables and nice cheerful music. Mosquitos can be a concern in the winter evenings but coils can be arranged. Our wait staff Nitesh was knowledgeable and Bartender - Anwar shaikh was good at his skills too.

Drinks/Beverages

We sat in the happening area by which I mean in the lower outdoor seating which made us order a cocktail and some mocktails. The cocktail was the kind of I like - With Bourbon Whisky. It is named as BOURBON HOUSE - it is a mixture of Jim Beam, Bacardi and Vodka. The beer glass with Jim Beam sticker looked amazing and the cocktail was even better. It was garnished with a slice of Orange and some leaves over it.

One of the mocktails we loved was THE HOUSE DELIGHT - According to them, they have it in different variety like Kiwi, Watermelon and some other options; we chose the KIWI based because Nitesh informed that it is the best of all and it actually turned out to be the best. It is a clear mocktail with in house mix with Kiwi as base with added soda, served in a Balloon glass. It had a proper not so sweet Kiwi taste. It is refreshing.

Food

Starters

To complement our cocktail, we ordered a dish to much upon. The all-time favorite and almost and the safest option - CHILLI CHEESE TOAST. It is just as expected and I am glad we ordered it. These were triangle bread toasted and topped with cheese, green chilli, onion and coriander (we requested to exclude tomato). It was crispy, spicy and cheesy at the same time and could be considered a perfect bar nibble.

The next dish is a perfect continental starter - GRILLED PANEER. We ordered this because The House is known for continental dishes. This is a perfect continental dish with Grilled paneer, mashed potato, Sauteed vegetables and Teriyaki sauce. I loved everything in here except the mashed potato as I am not a fan of potatoes. The dish is presented well, Paneer is soft and marinated well and the vegetables are boiled to perfection.
Mains

The House has a different concept in terms of main course. They don't have main course listed in the menu but they have daily specials which they write on a black board along with price. Out of the ones listed today, we went with the NAPOLEON PASTA - This is more of a white sauce penne pasta with a cheesy white sauce, exotic veggies and my favorite pasta bread. I so crave for these breads. Most of the times I agree to order pasta is because of these breads.

The pasta was Insta-worthy and hence available on my Instagram page too. The breads were a little soft and different from other breads that I have had, but we liked it too. Other items ordered were Pinacolada, The fruit punch & Venkatesh chicken. The house is listed under Rooftops collection. It has a smoking area and Wi-Fi too.

Overall nice place to chill, name_person=Deepesh Somani}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=3 years ago, review=We were looking for a good restaurant to have our team lunch. And when browsing Zomato, we came upon this and thought of having our financial-year end party here.

The restaurant is located on the 4th floor and on top of the evergreen building near the Khar railway station. The restaurant is not too big, but the layout is elegant, with a sofa-like seating arrangement at one end with a table in between. The restaurant also serves hookah for people who want to do it.

Coming to the food, we started with many sides and starters, including cheese corn balls, chilly cheese toast, bruschetta, cheese garlic bread, etc. Every item that I have tasted was one of the best I have ever tasted after visiting so many restaurants. But the chilly cheese toast and the cheese garlic bread were supremely tasty. The perfect cooking and the tons of loaded cheese on top made it delicious to delve into those.

For the main course, we ordered garlic naan, paratha, butter kulcha, and two portions of Veg. Kolhapuri and Butter paneer masala each. The Indian bread, all of them tasted excellent and were made really well. All of them were absolutely soft, and the amount of Butter on them improved the taste significantly. Each of the main course vegetables was delicious too. The butter paneer masala, one of my favorite main courses to try, was delicious. The paneer was fresh and soft, and the gravy was also not very spicy. On the other hand, the Veg. Kolhapuri was on the spicier side with a rich combination of delectable vegetables such as french beans, carrots, peas, etc.

We also tried out a few platters. I loved one Veg. platter particularly. It was a combination of veggies stuffed together, including Veg. lollipop and grilled potatoes, flame-grilled baby corns, bell peppers, etc. While the other was a Veg. starter platter that included two types of paneer tikkas (red and green), Veg and paneer Manchurian, and other starters.

There were also non-vegetarians in the group and what they tasted was also delicious is what was the feedback (since I am vegetarian so could not write in detail). Also, the restaurant staff was really professional, and they served the entire 24 member team well. All in all, I would say we thoroughly enjoyed our experience and would definitely recommend trying out the place. Visited Urban Tadka in Mulund West expecting a rich North Indian dining experience, but sadly, the evening was filled with more misses than hits. The vibe and branding promise a lot—but the food didn’t live up to it.

⸻

🍗 Happy Chicken Tikka – Underdone & Flat

The chicken was quite raw inside, with spices that felt slapped on rather than blended in. Texture was off and flavor didn’t settle. Disappointing, especially for something that’s supposed to be a highlight.

⸻

🐟 Fish Tikka – The Only Redeemer

This was the best dish of the evening. Perfectly cooked, well spiced, flaky and hot. If only the rest of the meal had matched this level.

⸻

🌶️ Garlic Chutney – Always Great

Still one of their strengths—bold, spicy, and garlicky. Goes well with almost anything.

⸻

🫓 Masala Papad – Shockingly Bad

I’ve had good masala papad here in the past, but this time it was very poorly done—soggy in parts, unevenly topped, and clearly rushed. It was a huge letdown, especially for such a simple dish.

⸻

🍷 Sangria – Just Syrupy Sweetness

This wasn’t sangria—it tasted like fruit syrup mixed with soda. No wine flavour, no balance, and way too sweet. It felt like a mocktail trying to pass as something it’s not.

⸻

🍮 Jalebi & Rabadi – Uneven Again
•	Rabadi: Thick, creamy, and well-made. A small win at the end of the meal.
•	Jalebi: Absolutely terrible. Not only was it soggy and bland, but it had a strong chemical smell—almost like bleach, which was shocking and off-putting.

⸻

💬 Final Thoughts

Urban Tadka Mulund is clearly struggling with quality control. From raw chicken and bad jalebi to sloppy basics like masala papad, this meal felt rushed and careless. The fish tikka, garlic chutney, and rabadi were the only saving graces.

⸻

❌ Final Verdict

Not worth the hype or the price. When half the items are badly executed—and one smells like cleaning fluid—it’s a red flag.
Urban Tadka needs to seriously rework their kitchen consistency if they want to live up to their name.

Would not return in a hurry.

The first dish I tried was Aloo Nazakat. This is a small appetizer with a good burst of flavors. It’s a small potato cut in half which is marinated with a spicy marination. Then it is topped with cheeses later baked in grill. I liked this dish mainly because of it size. I would say its like a small boom of flavors. I would recommend you to try this dish and pair it with a sweet mocktail.

The second dish was The Corn Cheese Kurkure. This is a very good veg starters and I would go for this dish over many non-veg starters. This is a crispy dish with a very creamy filling.
